summary: Misattributed early-access discount appearing on hourly embed batch invoice
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports an unexpected discount line on their finalized invoice for an hourly embed batch job run on 2026-03-08. The discount shows as 'Early Access Promo - NOVA' and reduced a provisional balance by 12.5%.

Impact:
- Invoice line reduced by ~12.5% for a single hourly embed batch run (~$1,800 credit).
- Customer is concerned this discount should not apply to dedicated customers under their negotiated contract.
- Customer requests either reversal or clear audit trail showing why discount applied.

Environment:
- NovaChat account: org_10291 (dedicated pool)
- Run: batch job id bch-20260308-76 (embedder-v2 microbatch, 120k embeddings)
- Region: us-west-2

Steps to reproduce / data to check:
1) Inspect postbacks for bch-20260308-76 for tags/metadata indicating promo eligibility.
2) Query postback enrichment log for discount tag mapping between 2026-03-07 and 2026-03-09.
3) Re-run rate apportioner for that hourly window to see if discount applied at aggregation stage.

Expected behavior:
- Negotiated dedicated rates should override any experimental/early-access discounts. Discounts should only apply when explicit promo tag is attached to the API key or account metadata.

Actual behavior:
- One invoice line shows a promo discount code 'EA-NOVA-2026' applied at the hourly aggregation step. Billing UI shows source = "discount-ingestion" and no explicit promo in account metadata.

Attachments / logs provided by customer:
- Finalized invoice (uploaded): invoice_2026-03-08_novachat.pdf
- Batch job manifest and job-level metadata (uploaded): bch-20260308-76-manifest.json
- CSV export of invoice lines (uploaded): novachat_lines_0308.csv
investigation_notes: 03-10: Ran postback replay for job bch-20260308-76 in staging postback-reconciler. Found a late enrichment message that attached promo_tag=EA-NOVA-2026 at 2026-03-08T23:47:12Z. This enrichment originated from the discount-ingestion lambda (logs ref).

03-10: Query against price-override table shows an entry for EA-NOVA-2026 with scope='global-experiment' and effective window 2026-03-08 to 2026-03-09. Entry was created by automation job promo-seed-runner with actor=deploy-batch-24.

03-11: Cross-checked customer contract (confluence link) — NovaChat has negotiated dedicated override row that should be prioritized over global promos. Contract id: CN-9872. No manual override record found in price-override table for this org. Suggests a precedence bug in rate-apportioner where global promos are winning over org-level overrides when enrichment arrives after initial aggregation.

03-11: Reproduced locally: run order of enrichment -> aggregation matters. If enrichment arrives after aggregation but before finalizer, discount_ingestion flag is still applied during the finalize step. Suspect race between postback-enrichment and finalization job (finalizer cron at :00 minute).
03-12: Added query links and raw enrichment log snippets to ticket. See logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/orgs/10291/streams/bch-20260308-76/enrichments

Hypothesis: a delayed enrichment message from discount-ingestion attached a global promo tag after the aggregation computed invoice lines but before finalization persisted the discount. Rate precedence logic then applied promo without checking contract override.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Aisha Patel (Support): Hi NovaChat — thanks for flagging. We are triaging and will follow up with an investigation. Can you confirm if any internal test keys were used during that run?
2026-03-10 09:45 - NovaChat (customer): No, we used production key key-prod-nova-08. Manifest included. We've attached the invoice. Please advise on reversal timeline.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Marco Rivera (Billing Eng): I've kicked off a postback replay and will post findings shortly. Initial look shows enrichment tag attached late — investigating why a global promo seeded to this org.

2026-03-11 15:18 - Priya Shah (SRE): Found that discount-ingestion lambda occasionally backfills enrichment messages when downstream metadata service is slow. It uses a backfill queue with best-effort delivery; backfills are timestamped with delivery time which can be after aggregation. We should not allow backfills to retroactively change finalized invoice lines without a higher precedence check.

2026-03-11 16:05 - Marco Rivera (Billing Eng): Agreed. Temporarily reverting the promo-seed entry for EA-NOVA-2026 to prevent further retroactive applications. Will prepare a corrective credit if this ticket is confirmed as erroneous.
2026-03-12 08:32 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer acknowledged and asked for provisional timeline for credit reversal and permanent fix.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: revoked promo EA-NOVA-2026 from global promo table to stop further retroactive applications. Short term customer remediation: provisional credit of $1,800 applied to NovaChat account as a ledger adjustment pending formal finance approval. Long term fix: change precedence rules in rate-apportioner to prefer org-level negotiated overrides over any late-arriving global promo tags; add check in finalizer to ignore backfill-enrichments with delivery_time > aggregation_window_end unless explicit admin-approval is present. Follow-up tasks: INT-8841 (billing finalizer precedence patch), PR #587 addresses ordering bug, add unit and integration tests for enrichment arrival ordering. Finance contact: Lori Nguyen for manual invoice adjustment. Customer follow-up scheduled: 2026-03-13 10:00 PST.

Finance to approve provisional credit and issue formal credit memo (contact Lori Nguyen, finance)
